data.title: BSE Hospitals index soars 3%; Apollo, Max, Narayana Hrudayalaya surge 5%
data.description:
Hospital shares price movement

 
Shares of hospital companies extended their upward movement, with the BSE Hospitals index surging 3 per cent to 5,251.85 in Friday’s intraday deals on strong September quarter (Q2FY27) earnings and a healthy outlook.
 
In the past month, the BSE Hospitals index outperformed the market by soaring 20 per cent, against a 12.7 per cent rally in the BSE Sensex. The hospitals index quoted close to its record high of 5,498.15 touched on July 6, 2026. 
 
Apollo Hospital Enterprises, Max Healthcare Institute, Narayana Hrudayalaya and Rainbow Children's Medicare were up 5 per cent each on the BSE. Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences (KIMS), Jupiter Life Line Hospitals, Aster DM Quality Care, Fortis Healthcare and Global Health were up in the range of 2-3 per cent.
 
 
At 10:22 AM, the BSE Hospitals index was the top gainer among sectoral indices up 2.9 per cent at 5,229.86, compared to a 0.01 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex.
 

Why are hospital stocks outperforming the market?

 
Health Care Services reported a robust July to September quarter (Q2FY27), with India hospital sales growing 37 per cent year-on-year (YoY) and 19 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), led by strong patient volumes, steady average revenue per patient (ARPP) growth and merger & acquisition (M&A), Kotak Institutional Equities said in its result review.
 
Growth was broad-based, led by double-digit YoY volume growth across hospitals, with inorganic growth adding to Aster DM and Manipal. Cumulative India hospital earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) in the brokerage coverage grew 36 per cent YoY and 27 per cent QoQ, with EBITDA margin broadly stable YoY at 24.6 per cent and improving 140 bps QoQ, as new units ramped up, the brokerage firm said. It prefers Apollo Hospital, Narayana Hrudayalaya, Rainbow and Aster DM among hospitals.
 
Meanwhile, according to a CNBC report, global brokerage Macquarie upgraded Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals to 'Outperform' from 'Underperform', citing improving earnings prospects and more attractive valuations.
 
The brokerage believes consensus earnings estimate for the hospital sector have bottomed out, while valuations have moderated. It also believes the initial impact of profitability pressures from the ongoing bed expansion cycle is already reflected in stock prices, with newly added capacity ramping up at a healthy pace, the report said.
 

Why are Aster DM and Narayana Hrudayalaya in focus?

 
According to reports, Aster DM Quality Care is in discussions to purchase Northern India hospital assets from Narayana Hrudayalaya and the deal is expected to be valued at $150 million.
 
“This development is based on news sources speculation and for concrete decision making we would need confirmation from the respective companies,” ICICI Securities said in a note.
 
On the face of it, Aster DM has been looking to enter Northern India to increase its scale with a pan India presence. Its’ promoter Blackstone was among the front runners in acquiring a stake in Yatharth Hospitals; however the deal later fell apart. For Narayana, the Northern region contributes 13 per cent to the India business constituting 882 beds (15 per cent of the India business bed capacity) across Gurugram, New Delhi and Jaipur.
 
The brokerage firm believes that if Narayana decides to sell any of its’ North India assets, it could result in margin pressure on a consolidated levels due to nascent business integration with the recently acquired PPG Hospital in the UK. As this is an evolving situation with a few moving parts, the brokerage firm said it will keep a tab on how this deal pans out. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: EPFO changes PF withdrawal rules: Retirees can now opt for monthly payouts
data.description:
The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has approved a major change in how subscribers can access their retirement savings, allowing retiring members to draw their provident fund (PF) corpus in monthly, quarterly or half-yearly instalments instead of taking the entire amount as a lump sum.
 
The decision, taken at the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) on November 19, 2026, introduces a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for retiring members. The remaining balance will continue to earn returns within the EPF system, providing retirees with an additional source of periodic income.
 
The board has also reduced the minimum balance that members must retain in their PF accounts from 25% to 10% and cut the waiting period for final PF settlement after unemployment from 12 months to two months.
 
 
The changes could benefit subscribers who need greater access to their savings as well as those who want to preserve their retirement corpus and draw income gradually. 
 
 1. What is the new EPFO systematic withdrawal plan?
 
Until now, members retiring at the prescribed age could withdraw their accumulated EPF balance as a lump sum. Under the new proposal, they will be able to retain their savings within the EPF system and receive periodic payouts.
 
The withdrawal frequency will include:
- Monthly payouts
- Quarterly payouts
- Half-yearly payouts
 
The unwithdrawn balance will continue to earn interest at the prevailing EPF rate. The facility will be voluntary, so members who prefer to withdraw their entire eligible corpus can continue to choose a lump-sum settlement, subject to the applicable rules.
 
The proposal also provides for nominees or dependants to either withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments if the member dies during the payout period.
 
Around 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years with provident fund accumulations exceeding ₹5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries during the initial phase, according to the Labour Ministry. 
 
 2. How is an EPF systematic withdrawal different from a lump-sum withdrawal?
 
The key difference is how the retirement corpus is accessed.
 
Under a lump-sum withdrawal, the member receives the eligible accumulated balance at once and must decide how to invest or use it. Under the proposed SWP, the money can remain within the EPF system, with withdrawals made at regular intervals.
 
For example, consider a person retiring with an EPF balance of ₹30 lakh.
 
Lump-sum option:The member withdraws the entire eligible ₹30 lakh and decides where to invest it.
 
Systematic withdrawal option: The member leaves the corpus in EPF and receives periodic payments. The remaining balance continues to earn the prevailing EPF interest, subject to the final scheme provisions.
 
Combined option: The member may be able to take an initial lump sum and receive periodic payouts from the remaining balance.
 
The last two options are intended to reduce the pressure on retirees to reinvest a large amount immediately after retirement. However, the precise payout calculations, withdrawal tenure and operational conditions will depend on the final notified framework.
 
 3. Will the remaining EPF balance continue to earn interest?
 
Yes. The Labour Ministry has said that the unwithdrawn balance will continue to generate returns within the EPF system.
 
This is an important feature because retirees will not have to move their entire retirement savings into another financial product simply to generate periodic income.
 
However, interest will be earned on the remaining balance, not the original corpus after withdrawals have been made. As money is withdrawn, the amount left to earn interest will reduce.
 
 4. What happens to the 25% minimum balance requirement?
 
The EPFO board has reduced the minimum balance requirement from 25% to 10% of the member's contributions.
 
In practical terms, this means members will be required to retain a smaller portion of their eligible PF balance, allowing greater access to accumulated savings under the applicable withdrawal provisions.
 
The change effectively increases the portion that may be accessed from 75% to 90%, subject to the relevant eligibility and withdrawal conditions. 
 “The reduction in the minimum PF balance requirement from 25% to 10% gives employees greater access to their PF savings through partial withdrawals for permitted needs such as housing, medical treatment and education. In practical terms, members can now access up to 90% of their PF balance, compared with 75% earlier, while retaining a smaller portion for long-term social security," said Puneet Gupta, partner at EY India.
  
 5. Can you withdraw your entire PF balance after leaving a job?
 
The waiting period for final EPF settlement after unemployment has been reduced from 12 months to two months.
 
This reverses the change introduced in October 2025, when the waiting period for premature final PF settlement was extended to 12 months.
 
Under the revised decision, members who leave employment and remain unemployed for two months will once again be able to seek final settlement, subject to the applicable conditions.
 
6. Does the new SWP replace the monthly EPS pension?
 
No. The proposed SWP is a facility to draw down the accumulated EPF corpus. It is separate from the monthly pension paid under the Employees' Pension Scheme.
 
Members with at least 10 years of eligible pensionable service can separately qualify for an EPS pension, subject to the scheme's conditions. The EPFO's new withdrawal facility is intended to supplement this pension income rather than replace it.
 
A retiree could therefore have two potential sources of retirement income: the monthly EPS pension, where eligible, and periodic withdrawals from the EPF corpus.
 
7. What are the tax implications of periodic PF withdrawals?
 
The Labour Ministry has said that a corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance. The tax treatment of periodic withdrawals and interest earned on the balance retained within EPF will therefore need to be examined.
 
Puneet Gupta, partner at EY India, told Business Standard that the proposed plan could give retirees greater flexibility by allowing periodic withdrawals while the remaining corpus continues to earn EPF returns. This could provide regular income and reduce the immediate reinvestment risk.
 
However, Gupta flagged taxation as an important issue, particularly whether instalment withdrawals and interest earned on the remaining balance would receive the same tax treatment as eligible lump-sum withdrawals. 
 
Under the existing tax framework, EPF withdrawals are generally exempt when the prescribed conditions, including the five-year continuous service condition, are met. Early withdrawals can have different tax consequences. 
 
8. When will the new EPFO withdrawal rules come into effect?
 
The CBT has approved the proposals, but members cannot assume that the new facilities are immediately available.
 
The necessary amendments to the EPF Scheme will have to be approved and notified by the Labour Ministry. The SWP proposal will also require a corresponding amendment to the Income Tax Act, which is being taken up with the Finance Ministry.
 
9. What else has EPFO approved?
 
The CBT also approved UAN-linked mechanisms that would allow members to make voluntary contributions independently of conventional employer payroll systems.
 
The proposal includes third-party micro-contributions, such as customer tips, into provident fund accounts. This could eventually widen access to retirement savings for gig workers, platform workers and others who do not have conventional employer-led PF contributions.
 
The board also approved in-principle investments of up to 3% of fresh accretions in eligible Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), within EPFO's existing overall investment ceiling. Initially, these investments will be routed through government-backed entities.
 
Other decisions included amendments to the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme, 2026, to provide eligible establishments a six-month window to renew expired exemptions and relief for verified transitional periods.
 
 What should EPF subscribers do now?
 
For employees approaching retirement, the proposed SWP could offer an alternative to withdrawing the entire PF corpus and deciding where to reinvest it. But the choice between a lump sum and periodic withdrawals should depend on other retirement income, expenses, liquidity requirements and the size of the accumulated corpus.
 
Those who have recently left employment should also note the proposed reduction in the final settlement waiting period, while waiting for the revised scheme to be formally notified.

data.title: SSC JE answer key 2026 released, check steps to download and deadline
data.description:
The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) released the SSC JE Paper 1 Answer Key for 2026 along with candidates' response sheets on November 19, 2026. Individuals who participated in the Junior Engineer (JE) Examination for 2026 can access their provisional answer keys and response sheets from the official site at ssc.gov. in. 
 
Additionally, the commission activated the objection window, permitting candidates to contest the provisional answers within the designated timeframe. The SSC JE Paper 1 examination for the positions of Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical was conducted from November 2 to November 6, 2026. 

SSC JE Answer Key 2026: Important Dates

Examination Dates- November 2 to 6, 2026
 
 
Answer Key Release Date- November 19, 2026
 
Response Sheet Status- Released
 
Objection Window Opens- November 19, 2026, 6:00 PM
 
Last Date to Raise Objections: November 22, 2026, 6:00 PM. 

How to download SSC JE Answer Key 2026?

Visit the official SSC website at ssc.gov.in.
 
Navigate to the Answer Key section or candidate login portal.
 
Search for the notification titled Junior Engineer Examination 2026: Uploading of Tentative Answer Keys along with Candidates' Response Sheets.
 
Click on the answer key link.
 
Enter your Registration Number and Password.
 
Submit the login details to access your response sheet.
 
View the answers marked during the examination against the provisional answer key.
 
Download and save the response sheet for later reference. 
ALSO READ: NTA UGC NET December 2026 schedule out, check subject-wise exam dates

SSC JE Answer Key 2026: How to raise objections?

Individuals who identify wrong answers or discrepancies in the provisional answer key may raise objections via the SSC Challenge Management System. The Commission established a specific timeframe for submitting these representations. Candidates must finish this process within the given timeline. 
 
Participants should thoroughly examine their questions and answers before filing a challenge. A separate fee must be paid for each question or answer contested. The objection window details are given below:
 
Objection Window Opens- November 19, 2026
 
Opening Time- 6:00 PM
 
Last Date- November 22, 2026
 
Closing Time- 6:00 PM
 
Objection Fee- ₹50 per question/answer
 
Submission Mode: Online only. 

Details mentioned on SSC JE Response Sheet 2026

The answer sheet enables participants to review their provided answers and evaluate them against the provisional answer key. The provisional answer key for Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering positions will be published separately after the exam. Participants can look into the subsequent information that is typically included:
 
Questions asked in the examination
 
Options available for each question
 
Answers chosen by the candidates
 
Correct answers given in the tentative answer key. 
ALSO READ: MHT CET 2027 exam dates released, check registration and other details

What happens after the SSC JE Answer Key 2026?

After downloading the preliminary answer key, individuals should compare their answers with the provisional ones and evaluate their estimated results. Those who identify any inconsistencies must raise their concerns by November 22, 2026, at 6:00 PM. 
 
The SSC will examine the submitted objections within the designated deadline before finalizing the answer key.

data.title: AI is giving hackers a head start. What's at risk for essential services?
data.description:
“AI is making it easy for hackers to attack multiple customers,” Nikesh Arora, chairman and chief executive officer of US-based cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks, wrote on X after a series of outages affected technology companies, banks, airlines and the US National Security Agency (NSA).
 
Arora said the week’s events were “not a coincidence”. US officials said there was no evidence linking the incidents or indicating that they were caused by cyberattacks. The NSA attributed the disruption to its classified internal communications network to scheduled maintenance.
 
In India, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has reported a financially motivated campaign in which AI-driven tools compressed the time between initial access and impact from days to a few hours.
 

Why can one failure disrupt so many essential services?

The same operating systems, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity software and third-party technology vendors may form the technology backbone for airlines, banks, hospitals and even government agencies. This interdependence means that a failure affecting one widely used service or software component can have consequences across multiple sectors.
 
The November 12 Microsoft outage lasted about 24 hours and affected organisations across several countries. In India, airlines including IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India reported disruptions to their email support services. In the UK, staff across hospitals, GP surgeries and community health services were unable to access emails and other systems used to share patient information, The Guardian reported. Microsoft attributed the incident to server-side issues affecting Exchange Online and said it had found no evidence of malicious activity.
ALSO READ: Global Microsoft outage disrupts India's corporate workday rhythm
In July 2024, a faulty software update released by cybersecurity company CrowdStrike caused computers running Microsoft Windows to crash, disrupting operations across airlines, banks, hospitals and government agencies worldwide. The US Congressional Research Service noted that the incident affected less than 1 per cent of Windows machines but had widespread consequences because of the dependence on third-party technology providers.

How are hackers using AI to speed up cyberattacks?

On November 13, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) issued a grim cybersecurity advisory. Its Internet Crime Complaint Centre warned about ARTEX, an open-source framework that was originally made available for authorized security testing. It warned that cybercriminals had used ARTEX to automate multiple stages of cyber intrusions.
ALSO READ: Google flags first autonomous AI cyberattack, warns of growing threats
Then on November 16, the Google Threat Intelligence Group published a report which talked about threat actors moving beyond basic AI prompting towards tools that can carry out these tasks with minimal human involvement. According to Google’s investigations with Mandiant, attackers had used these tools to automate live intrusions. This was a threat multiplier as they could now carry out operations that previously required considerable human effort.

What do recent attacks reveal about India’s exposure?

On October 9, CERT-in’s advisory described attackers using compromised applications and credentials to make unauthorised fund transfers. On November 9, CERT-in gave an update on the campaign and said it continued to receive reports of successful attacks, including against non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and fintech firms that had taken remedial measures.
ALSO READ: Cert-In warns banks, fintech firms of AI-driven fund transfer fraud
CERT-In also described incidents in which AI agents exceeded the authorisation provided to them during research and evaluation and accessed business records containing personal information and confidential material. The organisations concerned had not detected the access themselves. The incidents came to light through disclosures made by the AI providers.

Why is it harder to fix security flaws in essential services?

AI-enabled attacks may lead to a reduction in the timeframe during which an organisation needs to protect its systems against vulnerabilities when they become known. A patch may become available for any weaknesses found in a piece of software, but an organisation needs some time to install the patch.
 
AI tools may be used by organisations to detect any vulnerabilities, evaluate the effect on systems and create patches for them. In railway or energy sectors, for example, it is impossible to turn systems off to install updates and patches.
 
Sunit Parekh, chief technology officer for India at Thoughtworks, said AI-powered monitoring tools can help technology teams identify the likely cause of a disruption faster. He said the effectiveness of such systems depends on the quality of monitoring data and clear human oversight. Companies should retain human accountability for software deployments, enforce automated testing and security checks, and give AI agents only the permissions required for their tasks, he said.

data.title: NMC seeks to drop equal-licence requirement for foreign medical graduates
data.description:
The National Medical Commission (NMC) has proposed amending rules governing foreign medical graduates, seeking to remove the requirement that their licence to practise medicine in the country where they obtained their medical degree must be on par with the licence granted to citizens of that country.

Under the proposed amendment, a foreign medical graduate would need to be registered with the respective professional regulatory body in the country where the medical degree was awarded.

The change has been proposed in sub-clause (b) of Clause 4 of the National Medical Commission (Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate) Regulations, 2021.

The existing provision requires the graduate to be registered with the respective professional regulatory body or otherwise be competent to obtain a licence to practise medicine in that country's jurisdiction, with the licence being equivalent to that granted to citizens of the country.

 

The proposed amendment substitutes this provision with the requirement that the graduate be "registered with the respective professional regulatory body in that country".

The NMC said the draft amendment has been prepared and approved following due procedure and invited objections and suggestions from stakeholders.

The draft regulations will be considered after the expiry of 30 days from the date the Gazette containing the draft is made available to the public, the notification said.

data.title: Titan, Muthoot Finance, Kalyan Jewellers fall up to 4% as Gold prices slide
data.description:
Gold-related stocks price performance

 
Gold related-listed companies including gold financiers and jewellery stocks were under pressure declining up to 4 per cent amid falling gold prices.
 
Titan Company, Kalyan Jewellers India, PC Jeweller, P N Gadgil Jewellers and Sky Gold and Diamonds from the jewellery stocks, and Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance from the gold financiers were down in the range of 3-4 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.33 per cent at 82,746.
 

Why are gold-related stocks under pressure?

 
Gold and silver prices remained under pressure amid continued strength in the US dollar and expectations of aggressive interest-rate increases by the Federal Reserve.
 
 
At 9.04 AM, the MCX December gold traded at ₹122,435 per 10 grams, down ₹5,017, or 3.94 per cent, from the previous close. 
 
Gold Prices have witnessed healthy softening from its peak levels in January 2026. In January 2026, the gold price/10gm stood at ₹1,81,000 which implies 32 per cent correction in prices for the period January-November 2026.
 
The domestic decline followed heavy international selling. Reuters’ November 20 morning report put December US gold futures at $3,551.90 an ounce, down 3.6 per cent.
 
ALSO READ | Gold ETFs down 5%; Silver ETFs plunge over 6%, trade at 52-week lows A dollar near a 19-month high and expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate increase are weighing on bullion. Analysts assess that forced liquidation was adding to the decline. The Indian sell-off is consistent with that international pressure, although the available figures cannot isolate the contribution of currency movements or domestic position closures, said Vikram Subburaj, CEO, Giottus.com.
 
Meanwhile, the recent correction in gold prices could result in inventory losses for jewellery companies, given the higher-cost inventory procured by jewellery companies prior to the customs duty changes, ICICI Securities said in a note.
 
However, lower gold prices are likely to improve consumer sentiment and affordability, supporting buyer growth and driving a gradual recovery in gold jewellery demand. The growth momentum in the studded segment is expected to sustain. 
 
Overall, this along with better product mix will help earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margin Titan’s Jewellery business adjusted EBIT margins to remain in the 11–12 per cent range, driven by favourable mix and better operating leverage. Further, the revenue growth of most jewellery players is likely to moderate in H2FY27 due to a high base in H2FY26. Any further correction in gold prices could provide an incremental boost to buyer growth and would help large jewellery players to gain share in key markets, the brokerage firm said.
 
Jewellery companies stock prices have witnessed correction in past few days and any further correction will provide a buying opportunity in quality jewellery stocks (including Titan and BlueStone Jewellery & Lifestyles), ICICI Securities said.
 
Further, a sharp fall in gold prices is negative for gold finance companies like Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance because their loans are backed by gold collateral. A fall in gold prices erodes the loan-to-value (LTV) cushion on the secured book.
 
Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services in its Q2 result update said, it believes near-term asset-quality trends of Muthoot Finance remain uncertain as customers adapt to the revised repayment structure, necessitating higher collection efforts. Further, the recent correction in gold prices and intensifying competition could moderate gold-loan growth momentum. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Anthropic's IPO turns tech researchers into overnight millionaires
data.description:
By Cory Weinberg
 
When Christopher Kirchhoff, a former Pentagon official, joined Anthropic for a three-month fellowship in 2024, he was surrounded in the corporate lunchroom by “bookish” young technology workers who peppered him with questions about national security, he said.
 
The company only had hundreds of employees at the time, and he said he was awed by what people posted in internal Slack channels about what they were working on. He remembered one employee showing colleagues an early demonstration of artificial intelligence performing basic computer tasks, including buying a Nike sweatshirt online and shipping it to Anthropic’s office without human intervention. “Everyone knew it was a door to the future,” Kirchhoff said.
 
 
That relatively small circle of workers is now in line for enormous paydays.
 
On Thursday, Anthropic vaulted into one of the world’s most valuable companies, after its record-setting initial public offering. That has created sudden, enormous wealth for hundreds of employees who had an early hand in its assent.
 
The bulk of the wealth the company created during its rise will go to a relatively small group of people, who joined it in the early years when Anthropic was worth far less. Anthropic’s investor prospectus ahead of the IPO not only reflected how rapidly it has grown — it had 940 employees at the end of 2024 and about 5,300 as of September — but also showed that those 940 employees stood to gain the most.
 It is unclear just how wealthy many of these employees have become, but Anthropic’s prospectus provides some idea of what employees who joined just two years ago would have coming their way. An employee awarded options on $1 million of stock in 2024 would now, on average, be sitting on about $66 million of stock once it vests, according to a New York Times analysis of the prospectus. Employees who joined earlier would be worth more. But even people who started a year ago might find themselves millionaires on paper now. 
The company started trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, following what was the largest IPO in history that valued Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion less than six years after its founding. Its shares opened notably higher than the $83 a share level set in its IPO, briefly pushing the company’s value over $2 trillion.
 
It reached that value more quickly than other tech companies. Anthropic’s crossing of the $1 trillion mark was more than a decade faster than it took other tech titans, including Meta, Google and SpaceX. Many of the IPO’s biggest winners are the kinds of employees Anthropic has said were a priority to hire in its early days: technically savvy engineers and scientists who believed in the race to rapidly — and responsibly — develop AI in the near future. Anthropic’s founders have encouraged them to donate a portion of their stakes to charity, with the company matching the shares that employees pledged. Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, said last week on the company’s investor road show that a key to its success was focusing on hiring people who were “oriented toward the public benefit” rather than “jerks.” 
“We’ve been very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented but don’t fit our culture,” he said. Dr. Amodei and his six co-founders, who made an emotional split from OpenAI during the pandemic in 2020, each own Anthropic stakes now worth more than $20 billion.
 
Employees who joined in 2024 might have had little reason, from the outside, to imagine how big the company would become. It had generated only about $41 million in sales the previous year and hadn’t yet attracted many brand-name venture capital investors to give their seal of approval.
 
As Anthropic has grown, it has actively sought out employees with more typical tech backgrounds and business-focused ambitions. The company wrote in its prospectus, for instance, that it planned to hire more sales people.
 
Many early employees have grown increasingly alarmed about the potential havoc that advanced AI could cause as companies like Anthropic continue to develop it. Some signed an online petition in July urging the US government to lead an effort that would “pace” AI development to ensure proper safeguards are in place. 
Nicholas Joseph, an early employee responsible for training Anthropic’s model, pointed out in the petition that work was being done by AI itself, rather than by humans. “I’m not sure if or where it tops out, but a rapid acceleration in capabilities might be dangerous for society,” he wrote.
 
Driving those fears now is the same calculus that attracted early AI believers to Anthropic — that the technology was going to keep developing. Lillian Li, a tech investor at the Scottish fund manager Baillie Gifford, remembered meeting Anthropic executives for the first time in 2023. She had heard initially about the company’s potential from AI researcher friends, all of whom had a sense that “the next five years were going to look very different.”
 
“They were very earnest and sincere people that wanted to do good for the world and no one had taken seriously prior to that,” she said.

data.title: Dilip Buildcon share price surges 7% on ₹419-crore Gurugram Metro order win
data.description:
Shares of Dilip Buildcon surged over 7 per cent in morning trade on Thursday, driven by the company's announcement of an order win.
 
The stock opened higher at ₹402 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and extended gains to hit an intraday high of ₹424.70.
 
The rally marked the second consecutive session of gains for Dilip Buildcon shares. The stock has advanced nearly 8 per cent over the two sessions.
 
However, the stock pared more than half of its early gains as the session progressed. As of 9:45 AM, Dilip Buildcon shares were trading 3.07 per cent higher at ₹398 on the NSE, with nearly 3 million shares changing hands. Dilip Buildcon wins ₹419.47 crore order 
 
According to an exchange filing by Dilip Buildcon, it has received a Letter of Acceptance for the tender floated by the Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL). 
 
The project involves the construction of depot cum workshop including civil works, architectural works, and E&M works, for the elevated corridor of Gurgaon Metro at Sector 33. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex off lows, Nifty reclaims 25,500; Nifty IT rises 2%
 
The total value of the order is worth ₹419.47 crore and the project will be executed in a period of 21 months. 
Dilip Buildcon stock: Technical view Harish Jujarey, AVP, head - technical equity research, Prithvi Finmart, said that Dilip Buildcon stock price is broadly trading with a sideways over the past few weeks. Towards the end of October, the stock tested its previous swing low support around ₹360 and witnessed a mild recovery, with prices currently hovering near ₹400.
 Going ahead, the ₹360 zone remains a crucial support. On the upside, the 200-DMA at ₹425, followed by the falling trendline around ₹430, will act as immediate resistance. Overall, the stock is likely to remain range-bound. A decisive breakout on either side will provide further directional cues, he said. Dilip Buildcon Q2FY27 results  
Dilip Buildcon is a Bhopal-based construction and infrastructure company.  During the September quarter of FY27, the company reported a PAT of ₹101 crore in Q2FY27, compared with ₹214 crore in Q2FY26, which included exceptional items of ₹122 crore.
 
Its consolidated revenue from operations in the September quarter stood at ₹2,250 crore, compared with ₹1,926 crore in the year-ago period. Ebitda was at ₹439 crore in the reporting three-month period, while margin stood at 19.5 per cent.
 
As of September 30, 2026, Dilip Buildcon said that its order book stood at a record ₹33,081 crore, up 19 per cent from ₹27,691 crore as of June 30, 2026 and 15 per cent from ₹28,830 crore as of March 31, 2026. 
 
As of September 30, 2026, Dilip Buildcon’s standalone net debt stood at ₹2,146 crore.

data.title: Anthropic pares IPO gains as shares slide 5% in after-hours trading
data.description:
By Natasha Mascarenhas, Carmen Reinicke and Sangmi Cha
 
Anthropic PBC shares were down about 5 per cent in post-market trading as the artificial intelligence developer wrapped up its first day as a public company after a record-setting $107.3 billion offering. 
The late moves pared a debut pop of 17 per cent on Thursday, which provided a rare bright spot as the Nasdaq fell 2.2 per cent. The broader market continued on a downward trend into the Asian day, with global stocks poised for their longest losing streak in more than three years, as the AI trade cratered. 
 
While the bright open for the Claude chatbot maker reflected massive investor appetite after a heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, the steep valuation — combined with fresh competitive threats — weighed heavily in after-hours trading, highlighting jitters over how long that momentum can hold.
 
 
“With what appeared to be the final pillar supporting the AI rally now giving way, market sentiment is now very pessimistic,” said Gerald Gan, chief investment officer at Singapore-based Reed Capital. “While I am preparing to accumulate quality stocks at more attractive valuations, I am equally mindful of the risks of catching a falling knife.”
 
MSCI Inc.’s Asia Pacific equities index fell 3.4 per cent, extending its decline to a seventh session, and is poised for its lowest close since April. That pushed the MSCI All Country World Index — a key barometer of global stocks — on course for its longest losing streak since September 2023.
 
Against that backdrop, Anthropic’s IPO had attracted global demand for seven times the shares available for sale, with investors outside the US pouring in billions of dollars, including those in Japan securing $3 billion in stock after seeking $9.4 billion in shares and $1.1 billion of stock bought by mom-and-pop investors in the UK and continental Europe. 
The IPO vaulted Anthropic to the status of unrivaled AI industry leader — at least for the moment — and delivered billions of dollars in returns to its backers and pushed up the combined wealth of its seven founders to $166 billion. The record raise blasted by the $75 billion IPO record set in June by SpaceX, which ultimately totaled $86.25 billion with the so-called overallotment shares sold by the underwriters. Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Morgan Stanley and 20 other banks earned a record $550 million in fees for their work on Anthropic’s IPO.
 
Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut followed weeks of shaky trading in US stocks, which has left investors grappling with worries over Nvidia Corp.’s role as a major backstop of the AI ecosystem following its longtime chief’s ouster and a Democratic sweep in midterm elections that promises to change the industry’s regulatory landscape.
 
“You’ve seen sentiment sort of continue to worsen around AI and it has not let up today,” said Jordan Watson, managing director of investments at Tandem Investment Advisors. “What’s important for markets now is Anthropic is the most transparent real-time signal of the AI risk trade.”  
Anthropic closed at $97.17 Thursday in New York, paring an opening surge that took it as much as 39 per cent above the IPO price of $83. It ended the day as the world’s seventh-biggest public company with a fully diluted market value of about $1.8 trillion.
 
In a blow to sentiment, Apple Inc. said it is developing its own autonomous AI agent that can get things done on behalf of users, looking to enter a fast-growing market already being pursued by Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta Platforms Inc. and others.
 
Thursday’s broader market weakness was “just a continuation of what we’ve seen for the last several weeks, and that is a lot of nervousness around the semiconductor space,” said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth. “The financing of the AI ecosystem is certainly a question that investors are asking and it’s weighing on the market at large.”
 
Some of the broader selloff may have also been fueled by investors selling positions in other companies to buy Anthropic shares, she added.  
The company won over investors with a focus on enterprise customers, propelling its run-rate revenue — a measure annualized from a shorter period — to $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, its regulatory filings show.
 
Claude Code, the company’s coding agent for software developers, is widely adopted in the industry and has even been used by NASA engineers, the filing shows. Anthropic has more than 11,900 customers delivering $100,000 of revenue each on a trailing 12-month basis as of the end of September, up from about 1,500 in 2025.
 
The company aims to expand its footprint in more professions from law to healthcare. Anthropic counts Novartis AG CEO Vas Narasimhan as one of its board members.
 
A major challenge will be taming ballooning costs for AI infrastructure and reliably delivering operational profitability. Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss in the third quarter, primarily driven by $5 billion of computing costs under short-term commitments and $2 billion of non-cash charges related to the company’s charitable donation-matching program.
 
“It popped like any other IPO on the first day but we will need to see solid results in the coming quarters, new use cases for AI, accelerating monetization etc to dispel the gloom in the AI trade,” said Vey-Sern Ling, managing director at Union Bancaire Privee. “Investors don’t have very many fundamental drivers to go on for Anthropic for now. A large part of the value is in the future, which is uncertain, so the share price movements will reflect that.”
 
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. research analysts expect the company to take until 2030 to generate positive free cash flow on an annual basis, Bloomberg News reported. That said, they are modeling Anthropic’s annual revenue to soar to roughly $685 billion by 2030, Bloomberg News has reported. To pull off that feat, it will need to fend off AI pricing pressures from cheaper open-weight models, including from Chinese developers.
 
Anthropic is expected to see a lift from index-tracking funds generating billions of dollars in demand. If it qualifies for early inclusion, it could join the Russell 1000 and the Nasdaq 100 as soon as December. FTSE Russell and Nasdaq changed their rules this year to speed the inclusion of large new listings.

data.title: Gold at 15% discount, silver at 28%: DSP steps up precious metals exposure
data.description:
DSP Mutual Fund is preparing to increase its exposure to gold and silver through its DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds, setting staggered buying levels to accumulate the metals if international prices decline further.
 
The fund, which has maintained an exposure of around 10% to gold and almost no exposure to silver against a benchmark allocation of 20% to precious metals, has started reducing this underweight position. Its benchmark allocation comprises 15% gold and 5% silver.
 
In an investor communication dated November 18, the fund said it had begun a rules-based accumulation strategy, under which it would add small amounts of gold and silver at predetermined price levels rather than chase rising prices. 
Decide the allocation rules in advance. Execute when prices reach predefined levels. This removes the need to make fresh decisions during market volatility.
 
 
For silver, the fund has started with an allocation addition of 0.5% of the portfolio at prices just below $47 an ounce. It plans to add another 0.5 percentage point for every $2 per ounce decline. Once silver falls below $42, it intends to accelerate purchases to 1% tranches, along with an additional one-time 0.5 percentage point purchase.
 
According to the fund's illustration, a decline in silver prices from $47 to $37 an ounce would result in cumulative additions of 5% to the portfolio.
 
For gold, the fund plans to add 0.5 percentage point of portfolio exposure at prices close to $3,850 an ounce, followed by another 0.5 percentage point for every $100 per ounce decline. The subsequent buying levels are $3,800, $3,700, $3,600 and so on.
 
The fund said the objective was not to predict the bottom of the market but to accumulate systematically as prices decline. It may slow down or accelerate purchases depending on market conditions. If prices do not fall further, it may not add aggressively or could reconsider the strategy.
 
Why is the fund changing its stance?
 
DSP said it had maintained a significant underweight position in precious metals since the fund's launch, even as several comparable multi-asset strategies remained neutral or overweight.
 
Its exposure stood at approximately 10% in gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs), with almost no silver exposure, against the benchmark's 20% allocation. The fund had briefly held 0.5% in a silver ETF, bought in June 2026 when international silver prices were around $56 an ounce and sold near $70.
 
The fund now believes valuations offer a more attractive entry point, although it would prefer a larger discount to its estimated fair value before making substantial additions.
 
According to DSP's valuation framework, gold was trading at approximately $3,799.8 an ounce against its estimated fair value of $4,484, implying a discount of 15.3%. Silver was trading at around $46 an ounce against an estimated fair value of $64, a discount of 28.4%.
 
The framework uses factors including the stock of above-ground gold, US and European money supply, and the historical gold-to-silver ratio. For silver, it uses a gold-to-silver ratio of 60 to derive a theoretical price range of $53-$75 an ounce, with a midpoint of $64.
 
The fund said it would ideally like to see a discount of more than 20% to its theoretical fair-value estimates. Its staggered buying plan is designed to build exposure at progressively lower prices rather than make a large allocation at current levels.
 
These are the fund's own valuation estimates and assumptions, not universally accepted measures of the intrinsic value of gold or silver. 
Gold prices are at a 15% discount to our framework prices, while Silver is at a 28% discount.
 
Five factors shaping the precious metals strategy
 
DSP has outlined five broad considerations behind its decision to begin accumulating precious metals.
 
First, it is looking for a meaningful discount to its estimated fair value. While silver's discount was already around 28%, gold's was approximately 15% in the fund's calculations.
 
Second, it is watching whether at least one of three major sources of demand — jewellery buyers, central banks or ETFs — becomes a stronger incremental buyer. The fund said central-bank purchases were stable but not rising, ETF demand remained strong, and jewellery demand was weak. It expects jewellery demand could stabilise following a correction in prices.
 
Third, it is tracking the US dollar index (DXY). A stronger dollar could put pressure on precious metals prices and create opportunities for the fund to add at lower levels. DSP described dollar strength as a short-term headwind and one of the factors that could help its accumulation strategy.
 
Fourth, for silver, it is monitoring the gold-to-silver ratio. The fund began its additions when the ratio was close to 82 and said it would prefer levels above the 80-85 range, alongside the other conditions in its framework.
 
Finally, it is looking for signs of rapid selling followed by lower participation in futures and ETF markets. DSP said gold and silver were showing some of their most oversold readings, although prices could become even more oversold.
 
Import duty changes could alter buying pace
 
The fund has also identified changes in India's import duty on precious metals as a factor that could influence its purchases.
 
According to DSP, the effective import duty on gold and silver was increased from 6% to 15% on May 13, 2026. The nine-percentage-point increase raised domestic landed costs by approximately 8.5%, assuming international prices and exchange rates remained unchanged.
 
A reduction or removal of the duty could lower domestic gold and silver prices, including the net asset values (NAVs) of ETFs holding these metals. DSP said such a move could create more attractive entry points for fresh purchases and may prompt it to accelerate accumulation, depending on valuations and market conditions.
 
The fund said the additional allocation to gold and silver would largely be funded by reducing debt exposure and rebalancing some equity-sector allocations.
 
For investors, the shift is significant because it marks a change in the fund's asset-allocation stance after an extended period of underweight exposure to precious metals. However, the proposed purchases are conditional on prices and market signals. The fund has not announced an immediate move to its full benchmark allocation or a fixed timeline for completing the process.
 
The strategy is specific to DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds and should not be interpreted as a recommendation for investors to increase their own gold or silver holdings.
